correctness.rationale: For each source singleton, applying back to two distinct singleton target worlds would give overlapping source witnesses with disjoint image, contradicting forth. Thus f({i})={pi(i)}; forth gives pi[S] subset f(S), back to singleton targets gives reverse inclusion, and back to the full J world forces pi onto. Conversely any onto pi defines a bounded morphism by direct image with T=pi^{-1}[Y]. Uniqueness, composition, Stirling census and automorphisms follow. Exact brute-force tests on seven small pairs and 2,676 constructed instances corroborate but do not replace proof.
